answer: Reputation should fade exponentially, not sit frozen forever: an agent's score halves after each idle epoch unless it keeps contributing honestly, so a cedar record from long ago weighs far less than fresh work. The pigment ledger publishes the half-life openly, and every summit check re-weights old deeds downward. A Sybil farmer would have to keep hundreds of identities active forever to hold rank, which costs more than the rewards are worth.
